teacher_response.answer_text: An enzyme is a catalyst composed of protein or ribonucleic acid (RNA) [ev_001]. Most enzymes are proteins and perform the critical task of lowering the activation energies of chemical reactions inside the cell [ev_003]. A catalyst is a substance that increases the rate of a chemical reaction without itself undergoing any change [ev_001]. Catalysts work by lowering the level of energy that needs to be invested in a chemical reaction, that is, the activation energy, which is the threshold level of energy needed to break the bonds in the reactants [ev_001]. Enzymes do this by binding to the reactant molecules and holding them in such a way as to make the chemical bond-breaking and bond-forming processes take place more easily [ev_003]. Importantly, enzymes do not change whether a reaction is exergonic (spontaneous) or endergonic, because they do not change the free energy of the reactants or products; they only reduce the activation energy required for the reaction to go forward [ev_003].
teacher_response.short_answer: An enzyme is a catalyst composed of protein or RNA [ev_001]. A catalyst increases the rate of a chemical reaction without itself undergoing any change [ev_001], by lowering the activation energy needed to break the bonds in the reactants [ev_001].
